reason: This passage (Exodus 3-4) describes the calling of Moses and Aaron as leaders to liberate the Hebrew people from Egyptian bondage. Moses and Aaron, the leaders introduced here, are commissioned to help the people, not oppose them. The passage culminates with the elders and people responding positively: 'וַֽיַּאֲמֵ֖ן הָעָ֑ם וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֡וּ' (the people believed and listened), bowing down and worshipping in response to the signs performed. No antagonism between Hebrew leaders and the Hebrew people is evident in the text.
